Introduction and meaning
Dacoity (old 391/395): robbery by five or more persons conjointly. Attempt, assembly for dacoity, and belonging to a gang have neighbouring sections.
In student language: BNS s. 310 is the rule on “Dacoity”. The section provides that (1) When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, or where the whole number of persons conjointly committing or attempting to commit a robbery, and persons present and aiding such commission or attempt, amount to five or more, every person so committing, attempting or aiding, is said to commit dacoity. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 310 exists so that “Dacoity” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

The provision in detail
310. (1) When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, or where the whole number of persons conjointly committing or attempting to commit a robbery, and persons present and aiding such commission or attempt, amount to five or more, every person so committing, attempting or aiding, is said to commit dacoity

(2) Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

(3) If any one of five or more persons, who are conjointly committing dacoity, commits murder in so committing dacoity, every one of those persons shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

(4) Whoever makes any preparation for committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

(5) Whoever is one of five or more persons assembled for the purpose of committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

(6) Whoever belongs to a gang of persons associated for the purpose of habitually committing dacoity, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. (1) When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, or where the whole number of persons conjointly committing or attempting to commit a robbery, and persons present and aiding such commission or attempt, amount to five or more, every person so committing, attempting or aiding, is said to commit dacoity
2. (2) Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
3. (3) If any one of five or more persons, who are conjointly committing dacoity, commits murder in so committing dacoity, every one of those persons shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
4. (4) Whoever makes any preparation for committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
5. (5) Whoever is one of five or more persons assembled for the purpose of committing dacoity, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
6. (6) Whoever belongs to a gang of persons associated for the purpose of habitually committing dacoity, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Punishment / legal consequence
Life or rigorous up to 10 years + fine.

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 310 (Dacoity), Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:

   (6) Whoever belongs to a gang of persons associated for the purpose of habitually committing dacoity, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 310 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 310 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 310 unifies the definition (former IPC 391) and punishment (former IPC 395) of dacoity. When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, or where the whole number of persons conjointly committing or attempting robbery and those present and aiding amounts to five or more, every person is guilty of dacoity. The punishment is imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of dacoity under Section 310 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 310.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 310 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Dacoity (s. 310) vs Robbery (s. 309): The distinction is numerical: 1 to 4 persons commit robbery; 5 or more persons conjointly commit dacoity.

Dacoity (s. 310) vs Section 311 (Dacoity with murder): Section 310 is general dacoity (life or 10 years); Section 311 applies when any member commits murder during dacoity, making every member liable to death or life imprisonment.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 310 for conduct relating to dacoity.
Rule: Under BNS s. 310, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 310.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 310 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
